entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Takes a session and a user id and calls anonymize_user before committing.

stores.name: users

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: The comment on the column says the client sets arbitrary key/value pairs and that support pastes contact details in here.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name, so this column keeps whatever was stored in it.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: A soft-delete column; no code in the repository writes to it.

erasure.note: close_account overwrites email with its SHA-256 hash and full_name with the constant "removed"; the row, its primary key and metadata_json remain, and the hash still points at the address it was made from.

stores.note: Table holding the account record for each user.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: The comment on the column says the free text may contain phone numbers.

erasure.note: close_account does not delete the user row, and the tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so no delete reaches these rows.

stores.note: Support tickets, each carrying a foreign key to users.id.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: ip_address
fields.note: Read from request.client.host and written into the log line together with the request path.

erasure.note: Nothing on the close_account path touches this logger, and the repository contains no rotation or purge of its output.

stores.note: Logger named request_log, written once per request by the log_request middleware.

missing_entry_points.name: anonymize_user
missing_entry_points.expected: declare anonymize_user as an entry point, or say in its note why it is not one
